Man dies after stabbing in Mississauga
items.summary: A man has died after a stabbing in Mississauga early Sunday morning, and police say the suspect fled the area. m. on Sunday (Oct. 25) for reports of a stabbing. Police say one man was stabbed and later died of his injuries. The suspect fled before police arrived, and there is no suspect description at this time. Police say the stabbing appears to be an isolated incident. There is a large police presence in the area, and residents can expect road closures while officers investigate. The man’s identity has not been released. Anyone with information is asked to contact Peel Regional Police at 905-453-3311 and reference incident number PR260362288.

items.title: How to find your polling station in your Ontario town or city in Monday's municipal election
items.summary: Elections for municipal leaders such as mayors and councillors and for Ontario school board trustees are happening in 414 towns and cities across Ontario on Monday, Oct. 26. Monday, Oct. 26 is election day for Ontario’s towns and cities. Ontario residents are heading to the polls Monday, Oct. 26, for the 2026 municipal elections. ) are not holding elections as their councils are comprised of elected representatives from lower-tier municipalities. Not every Ontario town and city has in-person voting any more as many have switched to options such as phone-in or online voting. However, the majority of municipalities still conduct their elections through the old-fashioned paper ballot method at a polling station. They may also offer telephone, online and mail-in voting in conjunction with the paper ballot. The simplest way to find out where to vote is to check your voter information card. If you are registered to vote already (if you’ve voted in the past then you probably are), this information card would have been mailed to you several weeks ago.

items.title: Voter turnout in Peel region tends to be low. Meet the students trying to change that
items.summary: Voice the Vote, a student-led community initiative is working to address barriers to voting and civic engagement in hopes of reversing the trend of low voter turnout in Toronto, York and Peel regions in the upcoming municipal election.

items.title: Coroner Sets November Date for Inquest Into 2020 Death of Jamal Francique
items.summary: Insauga.com reports a coroner's inquest into the death of Jamal Francique, who died after an interaction with Peel Regional Police in Mississauga nearly seven years ago, will begin next month. According to Dr. Jennifer M. Dmetrichuk, the regional supervising coroner for the Central Region, the inquest is set to open on Thursday, Nov. 12. The outlet reports Francique, 28, died on Jan. 9, 2020, days after the Jan. 7 interaction with officers, and that an inquest into his death is mandatory under Ontario's Coroners Act. According to the outlet, the inquest will examine the circumstances surrounding his death and is expected to last 11 days, hearing from about nine witnesses, with the jury able to make recommendations aimed at preventing future deaths. The outlet reports Bonnie Goldberg will preside over the inquest and Roger Shallow will serve as inquest counsel, with proceedings held by video conference and open for members of the public to watch live online.

items.title: Peel Police Report 20 Per Cent Drop in Vehicle Thefts, Still Call Auto Theft a Top Priority
items.summary: Peel Regional Police say fewer vehicles are being stolen across the region, even as the force continues to treat auto theft as a top enforcement priority. According to police, 4,014 vehicles worth about $178 million were stolen in the 12 months ending in June 2026, down from 5,005 vehicles worth $257 million the year before, a 20 per cent drop in vehicles stolen and a 31 per cent drop in their total value. Police say thefts have fallen by 50 per cent since 2023, and officers laid 1,217 criminal charges tied to auto theft between January 2025 and June 2026. According to police, the force credits the improvement to strong partnerships, shared intelligence and coordinated enforcement, along with continued investment in prevention efforts. Police said in a press release that auto theft and cargo crime do more than steal property, underscoring why the issue remains a key priority even as the numbers improve.

items.title: London Police Charge Mississauga Man After Woman Reports Years of Exploitation and Abuse
items.summary: Insauga.com reports a Mississauga man is facing multiple charges, including human trafficking, after an investigation by the London Police Service. According to the LPS, the probe began in June when a woman came forward alleging she had been trafficked, assaulted and exploited starting in 2019, and investigators later learned the suspect had allegedly pursued similar relationships with multiple women over several years. The outlet reports police received information that one victim was exploited in the sex trade, that the suspect financially benefited from her activity, and that he tried to recruit additional women for sexual exploitation, with multiple incidents of violence also reported. According to police, members of the LPS Human Trafficking Unit, assisted by the Toronto Police Service Emergency Response Team, executed search warrants on Oct. 21 in Etobicoke and Woodbridge, seizing cash, four cellphones and a quantity of Percocet pills. The outlet reports the suspect, identified as 32-year-old Jesse Nigel Jones of Mississauga, was arrested in Woodbridge, remains in custody and is expected to appear in a London court on Oct. 26.

items.title: Peel Police Log Over 230 Distraction Thefts in 2026 as Gold Jewellery Remains Top Target
items.summary: Peel Regional Police are warning residents to be cautious around friendly strangers after a rise in distraction thefts across Mississauga and Brampton. According to police, officers have investigated more than 230 such thefts so far in 2026, with gold jewellery remaining one of the most commonly targeted items, and suspects typically approach people who are alone with what looks like a harmless conversation or a request for help before stealing their valuables while they're distracted. Police said in a social media post that not every friendly stranger has good intentions, adding that seniors, tourists, people who are alone and people carrying visible valuables face the highest risk. According to the outlet, police are urging residents to trust their instincts, saying that if something doesn't feel right, it probably isn't. The outlet reports one Mississauga senior told INSAUGA Canada she was approached by two people who asked for directions to a church and offered her fake jewellery to lure her closer while she was wearing a heavy gold necklace, but she recognized the attempted distraction theft and ran away.

items.title: Former Toronto Mayor Throws Support Behind Crombie's Mississauga Subway Push
items.summary: The Toronto Star reports former Toronto mayor John Tory has weighed in on Mississauga's municipal election, backing mayoral candidate Bonnie Crombie in the final days of a tightly contested race against incumbent Carolyn Parrish and councillor Alvin Tedjo. According to the outlet, Tory said in a Friday night interview that his experience working with Crombie was very positive and that she has the kind of experience cities need during difficult times. The outlet reports Tory also praised Crombie's proposal for a subway extension from Kipling Station in Toronto to Square One in downtown Mississauga, calling it a needed regional connection. According to the Star, Crombie responded in a statement saying Tory's confidence in her experience and economic leadership means a great deal to her. The outlet reports Crombie said that if elected, she plans to have Tory help lead her push for the subway extension.

items.title: Vancouver Resale Brand Mine & Yours Opens First Ontario Pop-Up at Square One
items.summary: Insauga.com reports consignment retailer Mine & Yours, known for selling pre-owned designer clothes, bags and jewellery at lower prices, has opened its first Ontario pop-up store inside Square One Shopping Centre in Mississauga. According to the outlet, the Holt Renfrew-partnered location marks the Vancouver-based company's third pop-up overall, even though its only permanent brick-and-mortar store remains in Toronto's Yorkville neighbourhood. Mine & Yours chief operating officer Danielle Loftus told INSAUGA Canada that the bustling GTA shopping centre suited a brand specializing in more attainable luxury goods, pointing to a strong emerging market for the luxury sector within the region. According to Loftus, the 13-year-old company already draws customers commuting into Toronto as well as buyers from across the country through its e-commerce platform. The outlet reports Mine & Yours previously opened pop-ups in Calgary last year and again this past spring, and the company has plans to open another pop-up in Montreal.

items.title: Crombie Makes Her Closing Pitch to Mississauga Voters: 'I'm Ready to Do It Again'
items.summary: In a campaign column for Policorner, mayoral candidate Bonnie Crombie writes that she is asking Mississauga voters to judge her the same way Hazel McCallion did when she endorsed Crombie's platform back in 2014, on the strength of her plan and her ability to deliver. Crombie writes that she spent the following decade putting that plan into action and is now asking residents to apply the same standard twelve years later, balancing ambition for a growing city with being mindful of who ultimately pays for it. According to Crombie, bringing the TTC's Line 2 subway into downtown Mississauga remains central to her platform, since she says residents need access to jobs without losing hours to commuting and growing neighbourhoods need transportation that keeps pace. Crombie writes that advancing the subway extension will require a credible business case, cooperation from government partners, secured funding and sustained pressure from a mayor who keeps pushing after the announcement, and she says she would bring Ontario, Toronto and regional transit partners together to move the work forward. She also writes that she would press to open the Hazel McCallion light rail line by the end of 2028, advance its downtown loop and improve bus and GO connections.
